purpose: Re-audit the current Ordivon project family as organs of one persistent adaptive loop, distinguishing local loop closure from persistent change, recursive improvement evidence, and autonomous problem selection.
claimBoundary: This audit does not promote a PAL controller, shared runtime service, protocol object, universal score, or open-ended RSI claim. It records current owner evidence and identifies bounded future falsifiers.

claimLadder.meaning: A physical or provider operation has identity-bound evidence. This does not establish domain value.
The owning domain can establish what consequence occurred and what it means for the domain objective.
Evidence changes a scoped explanatory/decision model, including narrowing or deletion.
The accepted delta changes a later loop's starting state, mechanism, policy, tool, retained evidence, or action set.
A later independent loop shows that the persistent change improved how future improvements were generated, selected, validated, recovered, retained, or transferred.
The system reliably discovers the next decision-relevant improvement pressure without a human/category oracle. Current evidence does not establish this level.

systemFindings: Ordivon does not lack feedback loops. It already contains multiple owner-local PAL organs and one bounded cross-evidence recursive self-reform experiment.
Computing experiment-loop-v0 proves bounded recursive self-improvement with third-generation cross-evidence-family transfer and rollback; it explicitly does not prove open-ended RSI.
Computing owner-pressure-discovery-v0 falsifies the current generic autonomous pressure-selection hypothesis. Reliable autonomous next-problem discovery remains unproven.

The strongest new audit distinction is therefore not loop versus no loop, but the ladder ExecutionEvidence != DomainOutcome != WorldModelDelta != PersistentChange != RecursiveImprovementEvidence != AutonomousPressureSelection.
Runtime, Host, and Harness should not absorb domain outcome or research adaptation semantics. Their current refusal to overclaim semantic completion is a PAL strength.
Cross-project adaptation should continue through owner-native evidence plus Computing comparison, not through a central PAL daemon or global owner-state registry.
Saved state is not automatically useful persistence. Persistence earns PAL value only when later work consumes it or it preserves recovery/selection options that matter.
Contraction and deletion are positive adaptation outputs. HR0, Security, Game, World, and Computing already provide examples where evidence removes apparatus or candidate abstractions.

Human-facing outcomes cannot be reduced to mechanical verification. Web, Studio, Game, and Human require UNKNOWN or sparse human calibration for comprehension, preference, trust, enjoyment, and normative value when those claims matter.

The current shared objective 'verified improvement per unit time' remains compatible with PAL, but recursive-improvement claims require later transfer evidence and cannot be inferred from immediate verified improvement alone.

worldModelDelta.previous: PAL was provisionally framed as a missing system-wide closed-loop/adaptation layer.
worldModelDelta.revised: Current Ordivon already has many strong local PAL loops and Computing already has bounded recursive self-improvement with cross-evidence transfer. The unsolved frontier is specifically reliable autonomous problem/pressure selection and longitudinal proof that retained changes improve future improvement across independent work.
falsifiers: A current existing owner artifact already provides reliable cross-project autonomous pressure selection under independent owner-bound holdout evidence.
A simple explicit human/Agent review baseline consistently matches adaptive self-reform and transfer at materially lower cost, eliminating the recursive mechanism's practical value.
Future PAL audits show that explicit future-loop evidence adds recurring bureaucracy without changing any retention, deletion, transfer, or research-priority decision.

nextFalsifiers: Persistence utility: on a real interrupted cross-session task, compare bounded Host checkpoint continuation against a strong fresh-owner re-observation baseline; measure correctness, repeated work, currentness errors and recovery cost without making checkpoint text authority.

Embodiment transfer: bind one Workstation-acquired scoped capability to a real downstream consumer outcome (for example World or Finance) and later test whether keeping that capability materially lowers friction or expands reachable work; delete/localize if unused.

Low-cost recursive transfer: in Game, carry one evidence-earned strategy/context/world-model delta into held-out Worlds/model families and compare against frozen baseline without compiling the answer into the planner.

Adversarial recursive transfer: use Security held-out opponent/world variants to distinguish genuine adaptation from evaluator exploitation or memorization before any coevolution platform is retained.

Creative prior transfer: test one Web/Studio prior earned by ordinary production on a materially different surface/Production, measuring bounded correction cost and objective craft/mechanical outcomes while treating human preference as separate evidence.

Problem-selection frontier: do not retry a generic selector on the same C6 corpus. Reopen only when a materially different owner-generated pressure signal or representation supplies a new independent falsifier.
recommendedDisposition: record_in_computing_research_only; no Core, Protocol, Runtime, Host, Harness, World, domain, or Workstation semantic change yet
